draft.title: Rural change
card: Many Australian farms have become larger and more mechanised. Fewer, bigger farms use machines and technology, so they need fewer workers.
When farm jobs fall, people often leave inland rural towns to find work. A smaller population can mean fewer customers and fewer students.
Shops, schools, banks and health services may then close or cut back. This can push more people to leave.
Not all rural places decline. Some coastal towns grow, as people are drawn by the climate, scenery and lifestyle.
draft.remember: Fewer farm workers can mean fewer people and services inland, while some coastal towns grow.

a.q: Why have many inland rural towns lost population as farming has changed?
opts: Larger, mechanised farms need fewer workers
Farms have become smaller and use more workers
Farm products have stopped being sold to cities
Machines have made farm work harder to do
a.why: Larger, mechanised farms need fewer workers, so people move away to find jobs. Smaller farms using more workers would keep people in town, which is the opposite of what has happened.
a.clue: Think about what machines do to the number of jobs on a farm.

b.q: The bank and primary school in a wheat town in western NSW close after nearby farms merge into fewer, larger properties. What is the most likely effect on the town?
opts: More people leave, as jobs and services are lost
More people arrive, as the farms need more workers
Little change, as services do not depend on population
More people arrive, as the town has cheaper services
b.why: Fewer farm jobs lead to fewer residents, and closing services gives people another reason to leave. The town does not gain people, as merged farms with machines need fewer workers, not more.
b.clue: Follow the chain from fewer farm jobs to fewer customers and services.

a.best: Larger, mechanised farms need fewer workers

b.best: More people leave, as jobs and services are lost

problems.detail: The wrong options are easy to rule out for Year 12 HSC students (e.g. 'Machines have made farm work harder to do'). A student could answer from common sense without knowing the idea of rural change.

a.q: Which order of events best describes decline in many inland farming towns?
opts: Farms mechanise, jobs fall, people leave, services close
Services close, then farms mechanise and cut their jobs
Farms mechanise, hire more staff, then the towns grow
People leave for the coast, so farms mechanise instead
a.why: The chain starts on the farm: larger, mechanised farms need fewer workers, so people leave, and services lose customers and may close. It is tempting to think people left first and farms then turned to machines, but that reverses cause and effect.
a.clue: Does the chain start on the farm or in the town?
